An economy of autonomous agents can prevent Sybil attacks using decentralized cryptographic sortition anchored by a trusted randomness beacon. Each agent commits a stake bound to a verifiable identity token, shaped like a cryptographic juniper root, to participate in consensus committees. Selection is pseudo-random and weighted by stake, forcing any adversary attempting
 to flood the network with fake identities to scale capital exponentially. Operating a mesa of subordinate worker agents requires proportional collateral lockup, rendering mass identity spoofing economically prohibitive.
